The default value is true.' refs claims.md:80 'you can use the MapInboundClaims = false option.' The realm file is Keycloak configuration and references no Đơn Hàng class.

The second arrow of the map rests on that reading, so the lesson should say it is one.

issues.text: Claims 1-2 (definitions of context map, upstream, downstream; arrow convention; attribution to Evans) stay unverified: content/versions.yaml has no DDD source and refs/ has no DDD mirror. The definitions are conventional, but no permitted source backs them.
issues.quote: the context whose model the other depends on; its changes reach the other side, not the reverse.
issues.fix: No text change required. Ask the owner to add a DDD reference under `standards` in content/versions.yaml (e.g. Evans' DDD Reference) so claims 1-2 can be checked; until then leave them unverified.

issues.text: The sentence says each context has its own words and that the two Status properties show it, but the lesson never says what values Order.Status holds or what Notification.Status means beyond one "sent" in the later code. I cannot see the difference I am told to see, so the claim that one API holds several contexts rests on something I have to take on trust.
issues.quote: each with its own words, as `Order.Status` and `Notification.Status` show
issues.fix: Add a short clause giving each meaning, e.g. 'as `Order.Status` (where an order is in its life) and `Notification.Status` (whether one email went out) show', or drop the 'as … show' clause.

issues.text: 'The email job' appears here for the first time, before the lesson says notifications is the part that sends emails. I could not tell whether it is the Notifications box, another part, or the refund job. Only the next paragraph lets me work it out.
issues.quote: the email job runs with no caller and reads no claims.
issues.fix: Write 'notifications' email job (the second arrow below) runs with no caller and reads no claims', so the job is tied to the box in the diagram.

issues.text: The text says ordering is the part that 'would call the gateway'. From the design-doc prerequisite I know the refund design calls the gateway from a background job, and this same sentence says a background job (the email job) is not ordering because it has no caller. So I cannot reconstruct why the refund job counts as ordering while the email job counts as notifications.
issues.quote: On the map, the arrow ends at ordering, the part that reads the claims and would call the gateway
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one saying the planned refund job belongs to ordering because it works on ordering's own data, unlike the email job; or drop 'and would call the gateway' here and explain the gateway arrow's end in the dashed-arrow paragraph.

issues.text: 'The meeting notes' are mentioned as if I know them. Nothing in this lesson or its prerequisite summaries says which notes or what words they use, so the motive of the second pull request is vague. It does not block the main idea.
issues.quote: renames properties of `Customer` in `Entities.cs` to match the words in the meeting notes
issues.fix: Replace 'the meeting notes' with a short concrete phrase, e.g. 'to match the words the business uses', or name one renamed property.

issues.text: The prose says the line 'turns off ASP.NET Core's renaming of incoming claims', but I did not know ASP.NET Core renames claims at all, or to what. I can follow the conclusion (the API sees `sub` and `roles` as written) but not why the setting is needed.
issues.quote: `MapInboundClaims = false` turns off ASP.NET Core's renaming of incoming claims
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying that by default ASP.NET Core would replace names like `sub` with longer names of its own, so the API would no longer see Keycloak's names.

issues.fix: Shorten c or lengthen one wrong option to a similar length, and reword c so it does not mirror 'as text checked at run time, as classes compiled against, or as a plan'.

issues.fix: Reword b to describe the symptom from a user's view, e.g. 'A staff member who could list all orders yesterday now gets refused, though the build passed.'
